mainTopic: Broken letters in תפילין, the crowns and shapes of the letters, and fixing a ספר תורה with mistakes
overview: This amud starts with two real cases of תפילין where a hole cut off the leg of a letter. רבי אבא rules by measuring what is left of the leg, and רבי זירא rules by asking whether an average child can still read the word. Next comes רב's famous אגדה: משה finds הקדוש ברוך הוא tying crowns on the letters. He sees רבי עקיבא's class, and later sees רבי עקיבא's cruel death, and each time he is told 'שתוק, כך עלה במחשבה לפני'. רבא and רב אשי then teach which letters get crowns and how careful scribes wrote the חי״ת and the הי״ת. The גמרא explains the shapes: this world was created with ה, which has an open bottom for free choice, a gap at the top for תשובה and a crown for the one who returns. עולם הבא was created with the small, bent יו״ד. The amud ends with the laws of fixing a ספר תורה that has mistakes. A ברייתא refutes רב's number of errors, and only missing letters count toward the limit. The amud closes with the case of אגרא's scroll, which had extra letters.

steps.title: A hole cuts off the leg of a ה
steps.stepSummary: A man's תפילין had the leg of the letter ה in the word הָעָם cut off by a hole, and he went to רבי אבא to ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: The leg of the ה in the word 'הָעָם' in his תפילין was cut off by a hole. He came to רבי אבא to ask if they were still kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells of a real case of damaged תפילין, and the man brings the question to רבי אבא. This sets up the ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ה is made of a roof and a leg hanging down. Here a hole broke the leg, so part of it is no longer joined to the rest. The question is whether the letter still counts as a proper ה.

keyTerms.meaning: leg (the downward stroke of a letter)
a hole or perforation in the parchment

phrases.english: The leg of the letter heh was cut off for him
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the man named just before this, רבי אבא's father-in-law. This happened in his תפילין.

phrases.english: in the word 'the nation' (ha'am), by a hole.
phrases.notes: שמות 13:3

phrases.english: He came before Rabbi Abba.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיפְּסִיקָא לֵיהּ כַּרְעָא דְּהֵ״י דְּ״הָעָם״ בְּנִיקְבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion on the daf about letters damaged by holes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is תפילין kosher if a hole cuts off part of the leg of a ה?

steps.title: רבי אבא: it depends on how much of the leg is left
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא rules that if the part of the leg still joined to the letter is as big as a small letter, it is kosher. If not, it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If what is left of the leg is as big as a small letter, it is kosher. If not, it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers with a measurement. Enough of the leg must remain attached to the letter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling looks only at the piece of leg still joined to the roof. If that piece is as big as the smallest letter (a י), the ה still has a real leg and is kosher. A smaller piece does not count, so the letter is broken.

keyTerms.meaning: the size of a small letter (a יוּ״ד)

phrases.english: He said to him: If there remains in it
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, and the corrected wording is in square brackets. Both mean 'remains'.

phrases.english: the size of a small letter, it is fit;
phrases.notes: The smallest letter is the י.

phrases.english: and if not, it is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִם נִשְׁתַּיֵּיר בּוֹ כְּשִׁיעוּר אוֹת קְטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question brought in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If the attached part of the leg is at least as big as a small letter, the תפילין are kosher. Otherwise they are פסול.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a practical measure for letters with a broken leg.

steps.title: A hole cuts off the leg of a ו
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר תמרי's תפילין had the leg of the ו in וַיַּהֲרֹג cut off by a hole, and he asked רבי זירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר תמרי, the father-in-law of רמי בר דיקולי, had the leg of the ו in 'וַיַּהֲרֹג' cut off by a hole. He came to רבי זירא to ask.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second real case like the first one, this time with a ו. This sets up רבי זירא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ו is almost all leg. If a hole cuts it, what is left may look like a י, and the word could read differently. This makes the case different from the ה.

phrases.english: Rami bar Tamrei, who was the father-in-law
of Rami bar Dikkulei,
had the leg of the letter vav cut off
in the word 'and He killed' (vayaharog), by a hole.
phrases.notes: שמות 13:15

phrases.english: He came before Rabbi Zeira.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָאמֵי בַּר תַּמְרֵי, דְּהוּא חֲמוּהּ דְּרָמֵי בַּר דִּיקּוּלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case of a letter broken by a hole, like step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is תפילין kosher if a hole cuts off part of the leg of a ו?

steps.title: רבי זירא: test it with an average child
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says to bring a child who is neither smart nor foolish. If the child reads וַיַּהֲרֹג it is kosher. If not, the word reads יֵהָרֵג and it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go bring a child who is not smart and not foolish. If he reads it as 'וַיַּהֲרֹג', it is kosher. If not, it is 'יֵהָרֵג' and it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא does not use a measurement here. He uses a reading test with an ordinary child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ו with its leg cut short can look like a י. Then the letters read יהרג, 'he will be killed', which is a different word. An average child shows whether the letter still looks like a ו to a plain reader.

keyTerms.meaning: neither smart nor foolish, an average reader
'he will be killed', a different word

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 2. רבי אבא measured the leftover piece. רבי זירא checks whether the word can still be read correctly, because a short ו turns into a י and changes the word.
steps.whatToRemember: A broken letter can be judged by how much of it is left, or by whether an average child still reads it as the right letter.

phrases.english: He said to him: Go bring a child
who is neither wise nor foolish;
if he reads it 'and He killed', it is fit;
if not, it is 'he will be killed', and it is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: זִיל אַיְיתִי יָנוֹקָא דְּלָא חַכִּים וְלָא טִפֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question brought in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An average child is the test. If he reads וַיַּהֲרֹג, the תפילין are kosher. If not, they are פסול.
steps.whyThisMatters: The test of reading by an average child is used in practical הלכה for doubtful letters.

steps.title: משה finds God tying crowns on the letters
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that when משה went up on high, he found הקדוש ברוך הוא tying crowns onto the letters. משה asked what was holding Him back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: When משה went up on high, he found הקדוש ברוך הוא sitting and tying crowns onto the letters. משה said: Master of the world, who is holding You back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the laws of letters to an אגדה about the crowns on the letters. משה asks why these crowns are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The crowns (small strokes on top of some letters) are linked to the topic of how letters must be written. משה's question means: why not give the Torah without these extra marks? This sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: crowns, small strokes on top of some letters (תָּגִין)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
When Moses went up on high,
he found the Holy One, Blessed be He,
sitting and tying crowns onto the letters.
He said before Him: Master of the Universe,
who is holding You back?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַב: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁעָלָה מֹשֶׁה לַמָּרוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the laws of letters in תפילין to an אגדה about the crowns on the letters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקדוש ברוך הוא tied crowns onto the letters of the Torah, and משה asked why they were needed.

steps.title: The crowns are for רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: God answers that a man named עקיבא בן יוסף will live many generations later, and he will learn mountains of הלכות from every tip of the crowns.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There is a man who will live after many generations, and עקיבא בן יוסף is his name. He will learn heaps and heaps of הלכות from every single tip.
steps.whatsHappening: God answers משה's question. The crowns are there because רבי עקיבא will learn many הלכות from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the tiniest mark in the Torah holds meaning. Some of that meaning will only come out through the learning of later great Sages.

keyTerms.meaning: a thorn, the tiny tip of a crown on a letter

phrases.english: He said to him: There is one man
who will live after several generations,
and Akiva ben Yosef is his name;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁעָתִיד לִדְרוֹשׁ עַל כׇּל קוֹץ וָקוֹץ
phrases.english: he will learn out from each and every tip
phrases.notes: 'Tip' here means the little point of each crown on the letters.

phrases.english: mounds upon mounds of laws.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אָדָם אֶחָד יֵשׁ שֶׁעָתִיד לִהְיוֹת בְּסוֹף כַּמָּה דּוֹרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers משה's question from step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The crowns are needed because רבי עקיבא will learn many הלכות from them.

steps.title: משה sits in רבי עקיבא's class and does not understand
steps.stepSummary: משה asks to see רבי עקיבא and is told to turn around. He sits at the end of the eighth row, does not understand the discussion, and feels weak.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Master of the world, show him to me. He said to him: Turn around. משה went and sat at the end of the eighth row. He did not understand what they were saying, and his strength grew weak.
steps.whatsHappening: משה is shown רבי עקיבא's בית מדרש. He cannot follow the learning there, and it upsets him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה, who received the Torah, cannot follow the Torah of a later generation. He feels weak because he thinks his own Torah is missing something. This sets up the surprise in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: rows (of students in the בית מדרש)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, הַרְאֵהוּ לִי,
phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the Universe, show him to me.
He said to him: Turn around behind you.
He went and sat at the end of the eighth row,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ מָה הֵן אוֹמְרִים,
phrases.english: and he did not understand what they were saying;
his strength grew weak.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, הַרְאֵהוּ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: משה asks to see the man described in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה sees רבי עקיבא's class, cannot follow it, and is upset.

steps.title: 'A law given to משה at Sinai' puts משה at ease
steps.stepSummary: The students ask רבי עקיבא where he got a certain law. He answers that it is a הלכה למשה מסיני, and משה is put at ease.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he reached one topic, his students said to him: Rebbe, where do you know this from? He said to them: It is a הלכה למשה מסיני. משה's mind was put at ease.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא says his source is the Torah given to משה at סיני. Hearing this, משה calms down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even learning that משה could not follow traces back to what he himself received. The later Torah grows out of משה's Torah and is not something new. That is why משה is at ease.

keyTerms.meaning: where do you know this from?
a law passed down from משה at סיני
his mind was put at ease

steps.whatToRemember: All the Torah of later generations, even the deepest learning of רבי עקיבא, is rooted in what משה received at סיני.

phrases.english: When he reached one matter,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי עקיבא, teaching his class.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ תַּלְמִידָיו: רַבִּי, מִנַּיִן לָךְ?
phrases.english: his students said to him: My teacher, from where do you know this?
He said to them: 'It is a law given to Moses at Sinai.'
His mind was put at ease.
phrases.notes: 'His' here is משה, who was listening.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: הֲלָכָה לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the worry משה felt in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי עקיבא's Torah is traced back to משה at סיני, so משה is put at ease.

steps.title: משה asks why the Torah is given through him
steps.stepSummary: משה comes back before הקדוש ברוך הוא and asks why He gives the תורה through משה when there is someone as great as רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה came back before God and said: Master of the Universe, You have a man like this, and You give the Torah through me?
steps.whatsHappening: משה has just seen how great רבי עקיבא is. Now he asks God why the תורה is not given through such a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה felt weak in רבי עקיבא's class, and then he was calmed when the law was traced back to him. Now he goes further. If רבי עקיבא understands so much, why is משה the one chosen to give the תורה?

keyTerms.meaning: Master of the Universe, a way of speaking to God

phrases.aramaic: חָזַר וּבָא לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: He returned and came before the Holy One, Blessed be He,
he said before Him: Master of the Universe,
You have a man like this
phrases.notes: He means רבי עקיבא, the teacher he just watched in the eighth row.

phrases.english: and You give the Torah through me?

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזַר וּבָא לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story right after משה was put at ease.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why משה, and not רבי עקיבא, is the one who gives the תורה.

steps.title: God says: Be silent, this is My plan
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא tells משה to be silent, because this is what He decided.
steps.simpleTranslation: God said to him: Be silent. This is what arose in My thought.
steps.whatsHappening: God answers משה's question. He does not give a reason. He only says that this is His plan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is not an explanation. It tells משה that some of God's choices are beyond what a person can understand. The same answer will come back later in the story.

keyTerms.meaning: it arose in thought, this was decided

phrases.english: He said to him: Be silent,
this is what arose in thought before Me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: שְׁתוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers משה's question from step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No reason is given. This is God's decision.

steps.title: משה asks to see רבי עקיבא's reward and sees his death
steps.stepSummary: משה asks to see רבי עקיבא's reward. He is told to turn back, and he sees רבי עקיבא's flesh being weighed in a butcher shop.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה said: Master of the Universe, You showed me his Torah, now show me his reward. God said: Turn back. He turned back and saw that they were weighing his flesh in a butcher shop.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward. משה asks to see what reward רבי עקיבא gets, and he is shown a shocking scene.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה expects a great reward for such great תורה. Instead, he sees רבי עקיבא's terrible death, with his flesh sold by weight like meat. This sets up משה's protest in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: a butcher shop, a meat market

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the Universe,
You have shown me his Torah, show me his reward.
He said to him: Turn back.
He turned back behind him,
and saw that they were weighing his flesh in a butcher shop.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִרְאִיתַנִי תּוֹרָתוֹ, הַרְאֵנִי שְׂכָרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: משה makes a second request after accepting the first answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא's 'reward' in this world is a cruel death.

steps.title: משה protests: This is Torah and this is its reward?
steps.stepSummary: משה cries out that such a terrible end cannot be the reward for such great תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה said: Master of the Universe, this is Torah and this is its reward?
steps.whatsHappening: משה protests what he just saw. It looks unfair to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The protest is a challenge to how the world seems to work. The more תורה a person has, the better his reward should be. Here the greatest teacher suffers the worst death.

keyTerms.meaning: this is Torah and this is its reward?

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the Universe,
this is Torah and this is its reward?

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ תּוֹרָה וְזוֹ שְׂכָרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the scene shown in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that God's plan is fair here.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Great תורה should bring great reward, yet רבי עקיבא suffers a terrible death.

steps.title: God answers again: Be silent, this is My plan
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא gives the same answer as before. Be silent, this is what arose in My thought.
steps.simpleTranslation: God said to him: Be silent. This is what arose in My thought.
steps.whatsHappening: God ends the story with the same answer He gave earlier. The story closes here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating the same words links both questions together. Why משה was chosen, and why רבי עקיבא suffered, both rest on God's plan, which people cannot fully understand.
steps.whatToRemember: Twice God answers משה with 'שתוק, כך עלה במחשבה לפני'. Some things in God's plan, even the suffering of the righteous, are beyond human understanding.

phrases.english: He said to him: Be silent,
this is what arose in thought before Me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: שְׁתוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers משה's protest with the same words as step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: God's ways, including the suffering of the righteous, are not always explained to us.

steps.title: Seven letters need three crowns
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that seven letters in a ספר תורה need three crowns each: שעטנ״ז ג״ץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: Seven letters need three crowns, and these are they: ש, ע, ט, נ, ז, ג, צ.
steps.whatsHappening: The story is over. The גמרא goes back to talking about the crowns on the letters, giving a practical rule for scribes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the story mentioned God tying crowns onto letters. Now רבא tells us which letters get three crowns. The seven letters are grouped into two memory words, שעטנ״ז and ג״ץ.

keyTerms.meaning: crowns, small strokes on top of a letter
a memory word for the seven letters ש ע ט נ ז ג צ

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of scribes to put three small crowns on these seven letters in a ספר תורה, תפילין and מזוזות.

phrases.english: Rava says:
Seven letters require three crowns,
and these are they: shin, ayin, tet, nun, zayin, gimmel, tzadi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שֶׁבַעה אוֹתִיּוֹת צְרִיכוֹת שְׁלֹשָׁה זִיּוּנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the crowns on the letters mentioned in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The letters ש ע ט נ ז ג צ each need three crowns.

steps.title: How careful scribes wrote חי״ת and הי״ת
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that the careful scribes of רב's study hall made a bump on the roof of the חי״ת and left the leg of the הי״ת hanging.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי says: I saw the exact scrolls of the study hall of רב. They made a hump on the roof of the חי״ת and left the leg of the הי״ת hanging.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds two more details about how letters should look, based on what he saw careful scribes do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a report of practice, not a new rule from a פסוק. The חי״ת gets a raised bump on top. The left leg of the הי״ת does not touch the roof.

keyTerms.meaning: of the study hall of רב
they make a hump or raised stroke
its roof, the top line of the letter
they leave its leg hanging, not touching

phrases.english: Rav Ashi says: I have seen
the exact scrolls of the study hall of Rav,
that they make a hump on the roof of the chet,
and they leave hanging the leg of the heh.
phrases.notes: This is the left leg of the הי״ת. It is written so it does not touch the top line.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: חֲזֵינָא לְהוּ לְסָפְרֵי דַּוְוקָנֵי דְּבֵי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more details about the shape of letters, after רבא's list of crowns.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חי״ת gets a bump on its roof, and the leg of the הי״ת hangs without touching.

steps.title: The meaning of the hump on the חי״ת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the bump on the חי״ת hints that God lives in the heights of the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: They make a hump on the roof of the חי״ת, as if to say: He lives in the heights of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why the scribes write the חי״ת this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letter חי״ת sounds like the word חי, meaning living. The raised bump on top points upward. Together they hint that God lives high above the world.

keyTerms.meaning: in the heights of the world

phrases.english: They make a hump on the roof of the chet,

phrases.aramaic: כְּלוֹמַר: חַי הוּא בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם,
phrases.english: as if to say: He lives in the heights of the world,

steps.triggerLanguage: חׇטְרִי לְהוּ לְגַגֵּיהּ דְּחֵי״ת, כְּלוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first detail of רב אשי's report.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bump on the חי״ת hints that God lives above the world.

steps.title: Why the heh's leg hangs: a question on a verse
steps.stepSummary: To explain the hanging leg of the הי״ת, the גמרא brings a question that רבי יהודה נשיאה asked רבי אמי about the פסוק 'בטחו בה׳ עדי עד כי ביה ה׳ צור עולמים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they leave the leg of the הי״ת hanging, as רבי יהודה נשיאה asked רבי אמי: What is the meaning of the פסוק 'Trust in God forever, for in יה is God, an everlasting Rock'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to explain the hanging הי״ת. It does this by starting a story about a question on a פסוק. This step only sets up the explanation, which comes later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The explanation of the הי״ת is connected to the word ביה in this פסוק. Here we only get the question. The answers come in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: in Yah, with God's two-letter name
an everlasting Rock, or Rock of worlds

phrases.english: And they leave hanging the leg of the heh,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדִבְעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה מֵרַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Yehuda Nesia asked of Rabbi Ami:
What is that which is written:
"Trust in the Lord forever,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 26:4

phrases.english: for in Yah the Lord is an everlasting Rock"?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִבְעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה מֵרַבִּי אַמֵּי: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the second detail of רב אשי's report, the hanging הי״ת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the פסוק 'כי ביה ה׳ צור עולמים'.

steps.title: רבי אמי: Trusting in God gives shelter in both worlds
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answers that whoever trusts in הקדוש ברוך הוא has a shelter in this world and in the next world.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Anyone who puts his trust in the Holy One, Blessed be He, has a shelter in this world and in the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי explains the simple meaning of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'צור עולמים' as a Rock for more than one world, meaning this world and the next. So trusting in God protects a person in both. This explains the plain meaning but not the exact word ביה.

keyTerms.meaning: one who hangs his trust, relies

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: כָּל הַתּוֹלֶה בִּטְחוֹנוֹ בְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: Anyone who puts his trust in the Holy One, Blessed be He,
has for himself a shelter
in this world and in the World to Come.
phrases.notes: This comes from the word עולמים, which can mean 'worlds', more than one.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּל הַתּוֹלֶה בִּטְחוֹנוֹ בְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Trusting in God gives protection in this world and in the next, learned from 'עולמים'.

steps.title: רבי יהודה נשיאה clarifies: Why ביה and not יה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה נשיאה says that is not what bothers him. His real question is why the פסוק says ביה, 'in Yah', and not just יה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what is hard for me: why is it written ביה and not written יה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה נשיאה explains that רבי אמי answered the wrong question. He sharpens his question to focus on one extra letter. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra letter ב, meaning 'in', seems unnecessary. The פסוק could just have said יה. This question about the word itself will lead to the explanation of the hanging הי״ת.

keyTerms.meaning: a difficulty, what is hard to understand
what is different, why this way
a two-letter name of God, made of י and ה

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה נשיאה is not rejecting רבי אמי's idea. He is saying that his question was about the exact word ביה, not about the general meaning of the פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא הָכִי קָא קַשְׁיָא לִי,
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what is difficult for me,
what is different that it is written "in Yah"
and it is not written "Yah"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנָא הָכִי קָא קַשְׁיָא לִי, מַאי שְׁנָא דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains that step 18 did not address the real question and narrows it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק uses ביה with an extra ב instead of just יה.

steps.title: The two letters of יה stand for two worlds
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר רבי אילעאי teaches that the letters of יה stand for two worlds God created, one with ה and one with י, but he does not know which world goes with which letter.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יהודה בר רבי אילעאי taught: these letters stand for the two worlds that הקדוש ברוך הוא created, one with ה and one with י. And I don't know whether עולם הבא was made with י and עולם הזה with ה, or עולם הזה with י and עולם הבא with ה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי יהודה נשיאה's question about why the פסוק says ביה. The extra ב means 'with', so the פסוק is saying God created the worlds with the letters י and ה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words צור עולמים are read as 'Creator of worlds', and ביה is read as 'with the letters י and ה'. So the פסוק teaches that each world was made with one of these letters. רבי יהודה בר רבי אילעאי is not yet sure which letter goes with which world. The next step settles this.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught or explained a פסוק in a deeper way

phrases.aramaic: כִּדְדָרֵשׁ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר רַבִּי אִילְעַאי:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Yehuda bar Rabbi Elai taught:
These are the two worlds
phrases.notes: 'These' means the two letters י and ה in the word ביה, which the פסוק links to צור עולמים, 'Creator of worlds'.

phrases.english: that the Holy One, Blessed be He, created,
one with the letter heh and one with the letter yod.
And I do not know
whether the World to Come was made with yod
and this world with heh,
or whether this world was made with yod
and the World to Come with heh.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְדָרֵשׁ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר רַבִּי אִילְעַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19 about why the פסוק says ביה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ב means 'with': the two worlds were created with the letters י and ה.

steps.title: A פסוק shows this world was created with ה
steps.stepSummary: Reading בהבראם as 'בה״י בראם', 'He created them with ה', proves that heaven and earth (this world) were made with the letter ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the פסוק says 'These are the generations of the heaven and the earth when they were created (בהבראם)', don't read it as בהבראם. Read it as 'בה״י בראם', 'with ה He created them'.
steps.whatsHappening: The doubt from the previous step is settled with a פסוק. Heaven and earth, which are this world, were created with ה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בהבראם is split into ב-ה and בראם, giving 'with ה He created them'. Since this world goes with ה, עולם הבא must go with י.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't read it as..., a way of reading a word differently to learn something from it

phrases.english: When it says:
"These are the generations of the heaven and the earth
phrases.notes: בראשית 2:4

phrases.english: when they were created,"
do not read it as "when they were created"
but rather: "with heh He created them."
phrases.notes: The same letters are split into two words, 'with ה' and 'He created them', so heaven and earth were made with ה.

steps.whatToRemember: עולם הזה was created with ה, and עולם הבא with י.
steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the doubt left open in step 20
steps.raayaObject: That this world was created with ה
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 2:4, בהבראם read as בה״י בראם

steps.title: Why was this world made with ה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this world specifically was created with the letter ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why was this world created with ה?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know this world was made with ה, the גמרא asks what the reason is. It is setting up an explanation based on the shape of the letter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question moves from which letter to why that letter. The answer will connect the shape of ה to how life works in this world.

phrases.english: And for what reason
was this world created with heh?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּהֵ״י
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the fact proven in step 21
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason this world was created with ה

steps.title: The ה is open like a porch
steps.stepSummary: The ה is open at the bottom like a porch, which shows that in this world anyone who wants to leave can leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it looks like a porch: anyone who wants to go out can go out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ה is open at the bottom, like a porch that has an open side. This stands for the freedom in this world to walk away and choose wrongdoing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The open bottom of the ה is the picture of free choice. In this world nothing stops a person from leaving the right path.

keyTerms.meaning: A porch or portico, a covered area with an open side
Whoever wants to leave may leave

phrases.english: Because it looks like a porch,
where anyone who wants to leave may leave.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁדּוֹמֶה לְאַכְסַדְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The open bottom of the ה shows that in this world anyone can leave, meaning anyone can choose to sin.

steps.title: Why does the leg of the ה hang loose?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the left leg of the ה is not attached to its roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why does its leg hang?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about the hanging leg of the ה that the scribes made, as reported in step 15. This is the detail the whole discussion set out to explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The open bottom has already been explained. Now the גמרא asks about the second opening, the gap at the top between the leg and the roof.

phrases.english: And what is the reason its leg hangs?
phrases.notes: This is the left leg of the ה, which doesn't touch the roof and leaves a gap at the top.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי טַעְמָא תַּלְיָא כַּרְעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the hanging leg mentioned in step 15
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the gap between the ה's left leg and its roof

steps.title: The gap at the top lets the one who does תשובה back in
steps.stepSummary: If a person does תשובה, he is brought back in through the opening at the top of the ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if he comes back in תשובה, they bring him in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the gap at the top is a special way back in for someone who does תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person leaves through the bottom, but returns through a separate opening at the top. This shows that the way back is a door God opens for the returning sinner.

phrases.english: Because if he returns in repentance,
they bring him in.
phrases.notes: He is brought in through the gap at the top of the ה.

steps.whatToRemember: The ה has two openings: the bottom is where a person leaves through sin, and the top gap is where he comes back through תשובה.
steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי הָדַר בִּתְשׁוּבָה מְעַיְּילִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The gap at the top is the entrance for one who does תשובה.

steps.title: Why not come back in the same way he left?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: let the returning person come back in through the bottom opening, the same way he went out.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him come in through that one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea of a separate top entrance. If the bottom is open, why not return that way? This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is that a second opening seems unnecessary when the first one is already open. The גמרא wants to know what the top gap adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Through that one, the bottom opening

phrases.english: But let him enter through that one!
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the open bottom of the ה, the way he went out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיעַיֵּיל בְּהָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the top entrance described in step 25
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the returning sinner needs a separate entrance at the top
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bottom is already open, so a second opening seems unneeded.

steps.title: Coming back needs help from Heaven
steps.stepSummary: Returning the same way would not work on its own. Following ריש לקיש, one who wants to become pure is helped from Heaven, while one who wants to become impure is only given an opening.
steps.simpleTranslation: It would not work out. As ריש לקיש said: what does the פסוק 'If it concerns the scorners, He scorns them, and to the humble He gives grace' mean? One who comes to become pure is helped; one who comes to become impure is given an opening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that returning is not as easy as leaving. A person needs special help from above, which is why there is a separate entrance at the top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving only needs an open door, so the bottom of the ה is simply open. Coming back needs active help from Heaven, and that help is pictured as the top entrance where God brings him in.

keyTerms.meaning: It would not succeed, it would not work out
They open the way for him

phrases.english: It would not work out,
in line with Reish Lakish, for Reish Lakish said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"If it concerns the scorners, He scorns them,
phrases.notes: משלי 3:34

phrases.english: and to the humble He gives grace"?
One who comes to become pure is helped,
one who comes to become impure is given an opening.

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש does not mean God pushes anyone to sin. The sinner is only given an open door, while the one returning gets real help.
steps.triggerLanguage: לָא מִסְתַּיְּיעָא מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a source showing that returning needs help from Heaven
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Returning is as simple as leaving, so the same opening would be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: Returning needs help from Heaven, so it has its own entrance at the top where God brings him in.

steps.title: Why does the ה have a crown?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ה has a crown on its roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why does it have a crown?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about one more feature of the ה, the small crown drawn on top of it. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After explaining the two openings, the גמרא turns to the decoration on the roof of the letter.

keyTerms.meaning: A crown, a small decoration on top of a letter

phrases.english: And what is the reason it has a crown?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי טַעְמָא אִית לֵיהּ תָּאגָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about another feature of the ה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the crown on the ה

steps.title: God ties a crown for the one who returns
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא says: if the sinner returns, I tie a crown for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא says: if he returns, I tie a knot (a crown) for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the crown stands for the honor God gives a person who does תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The crown sits right above the top entrance where the returning person comes in. He is not only let back in, he is crowned by God.

keyTerms.meaning: Ties a knot for him, here meaning a crown

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם חוֹזֵר – אֲנִי קוֹשֵׁר לוֹ קֶשֶׁר.
phrases.english: If he returns, I tie a knot for him.
phrases.notes: The 'knot' is the crown on top of the ה, tied on as an honor for the one who returns.

steps.whatToRemember: Every part of the ה tells a story: the open bottom is free choice, the top gap is the way back through תשובה, and the crown is the honor God gives the one who returns.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: אִם חוֹזֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The crown shows that God crowns the one who does תשובה.

steps.title: Why was the עולם הבא created with a יו״ד?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the עולם הבא was created with the letter יו״ד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why was the עולם הבא created with the letter יו״ד?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its explanation of letter shapes and now asks about the יו״ד, the letter used to create the עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא explained the shape of the ה, the letter used for this world. Now it asks the same kind of question about the יו״ד. The יו״ד is the smallest letter, so the question is what that small size teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: The letter י, the smallest letter of the אלף-בית

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא בְּיוֹ״ד?
phrases.english: For what reason was the World-to-Come created with a yod?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא בְּיוֹ״ד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ה of this world to the יו״ד of the World-to-Come.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the small יו״ד teaches about the עולם הבא.

steps.title: Because the righteous are few
steps.stepSummary: The יו״ד is small because the צדיקים are few.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the righteous in it are few.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the small letter matches the small number of צדיקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The size of the letter hints at how many people will be in the World-to-Come. A tiny letter stands for a small group of truly righteous people.

phrases.english: Because the righteous in it are few.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁבּוֹ מוּעָטִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The small size of the יו״ד hints that the צדיקים are few.

steps.title: Why is the top of the יו״ד bent?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the head of the יו״ד is bent down.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is its head bent?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about another detail of the יו״ד's shape.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The size of the letter has been explained. Now the גמרא wants to know what the bent top of the letter teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Its head (here, the top of the letter)

phrases.english: And for what reason is its head bent?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה כָּפוּף רֹאשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a second feature of the same letter.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the bent top of the יו״ד hints at.

steps.title: The righteous bow their heads because their deeds are not equal
steps.stepSummary: The צדיקים in the עולם הבא bow their heads because their deeds differ from one another.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the righteous there bow their heads on account of their deeds, since one person's deeds are not like another's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the bent head stands for the צדיקים lowering their heads in the World-to-Come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even among the צדיקים, some did more than others. When this becomes clear, the ones who did less bow their heads in shame. The bent letter is a picture of that.
steps.whatToRemember: The ה stands for this world, with an opening for תשובה. The small, bent יו״ד stands for the World-to-Come, where few people are truly righteous and their levels are not equal.

phrases.english: Because the righteous in it, their heads are bent
on account of their deeds,
since they are not like one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁבּוֹ כָּפוּף רָאשֵׁיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 32 and closes the אגדה about letter shapes.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The bent head shows the צדיקים bowing in shame, because their deeds are not equal.

steps.title: רב יוסף: two rulings of רב about scrolls, each refuted
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף announces that רב made two rulings about scrolls, and a ברייתא refutes each one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: רב said these two things about scrolls, and a ברייתא was taught that refutes him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new הלכה topic. רב יוסף is setting up the next steps by telling us two rulings of רב are coming, each with a ברייתא against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line is an introduction. It does not give a ruling yet. It only tells us what to expect: two statements of רב about writing ספרים, each challenged by a ברייתא. The first one comes right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Scrolls (holy books such as a ספר תורה)

steps.confusionAlert: This line only announces the refutations. The actual ברייתא that argues with רב comes a few lines later, in step 36.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef says:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי תַּרְתֵּי מִילֵּי אָמַר רַב בִּסְפָרִים,
phrases.english: These two matters, Rav said regarding scrolls,
and a baraita is taught that refutes him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי תַּרְתֵּי מִילֵּי אָמַר רַב בִּסְפָרִים וְתַנְיָא תְּיוּבְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה and opens a new section about the laws of writing a ספר תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two rulings of רב about scrolls are each opposed by a ברייתא.

steps.title: רב: two errors per column can be fixed, three means the scroll is put away
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a ספר תורה with two mistakes on every column may be fixed, but one with three should be put away (נגנז).
steps.simpleTranslation: The first is what רב said: a ספר תורה with two errors on each column may be corrected. With three errors, it should be put away.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first of רב's two rulings. It sets the limit of mistakes for fixing a ספר תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mistakes in a ספר תורה can usually be corrected. But if a scroll is full of mistakes, רב says it is not fixed. It is put away instead (גניזה). For רב the line is three mistakes on every column.

keyTerms.meaning: Column of writing in the scroll
It should be put away (stored respectfully, not used)

phrases.english: One is that which Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ שְׁתֵּי טָעִיּוֹת
phrases.english: A Torah scroll that has in it two errors
on each and every column may be corrected;
phrases.notes: Here דַּף means a column of writing on the scroll, not a page of גמרא.

phrases.english: with three, it shall be put away.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first of the two rulings announced in step 34.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two errors per column may be fixed. Three errors per column means גניזה.

steps.title: The ברייתא: three errors can be fixed, four means put away
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא disagrees with רב: three mistakes per column may still be fixed. Only four require גניזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא refutes him: with three, he may correct it. With four, it should be put away.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the ברייתא that רב יוסף promised. It argues with רב's number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said three mistakes is already too many. The ברייתא allows three and only puts the scroll away at four. רב יוסף calls this ברייתא a refutation (תיובתא) of רב's ruling.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's rule: up to three mistakes per column, fix the scroll. Four on every column, put it away.

phrases.english: And a baraita is taught that refutes him:
Three, he may correct; four, it shall be put away.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא תְּיוּבְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling in step 35 with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that three errors per column requires גניזה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly allows fixing a scroll with three errors per column and requires גניזה only at four.

steps.title: One perfect column saves the whole scroll
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if the scroll has one column with no mistakes, the whole scroll may be fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: if it has one complete column, it saves the whole scroll.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another ברייתא that softens the rule. One perfect column stops the scroll from being put away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limit is about mistakes on every single column. If even one column has no errors, the scroll is not considered full of mistakes, so it may be corrected instead of put away.

keyTerms.meaning: Complete, here meaning with no errors
All of it, the entire scroll

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: אִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ דַּף אַחַת שְׁלֵימָה –
phrases.english: It was taught: If there is in it one complete column,
it saves the whole of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא אִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ דַּף אַחַת שְׁלֵימָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the rule of how many errors lead to גניזה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One error-free column lets the entire scroll be fixed.

steps.title: Only if most of the scroll is written well
steps.stepSummary: In רב's name: the perfect column saves the scroll only when most of the scroll is written properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא said in the name of רב: this is only when most of the scroll is written properly.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא limits the rule of step 37. One good column helps only if most of the scroll is in good shape.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this limit, one good column could save a scroll that is almost entirely wrong. רב says the column helps only when most of the text is written correctly.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is only when, a phrase that adds a condition

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta said in the name of Rav:
And this is when most of the scroll is written properly.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהוּא דִּכְתִיב רוּבֵּיהּ דְּסִפְרָא שַׁפִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts a condition on the ברייתא of step 37.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The one good column saves the scroll only if most of the scroll is written correctly.

steps.title: אביי: what if that column has three errors?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף what the law is if the column that is supposed to save the scroll itself has three mistakes.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: if that column has three errors, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a follow-up question. The rest of the scroll has four errors on each column, and one column has only three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three errors is still fixable according to the ברייתא, but that column is not perfect. אביי wants to know whether such a column can still save the whole scroll the way a perfect column does.

keyTerms.meaning: That column (the one meant to save the scroll)

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אִית בְּהָהוּא דַּף שָׁלֹשׁ טָעִיּוֹת, מַאי?
phrases.english: If there are three errors in that column, what?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אִית בְּהָהוּא דַּף שָׁלֹשׁ טָעִיּוֹת מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the limits of the 'one complete column' rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a column with three fixable errors counts as a 'complete' column that saves the scroll.

steps.title: Since it can be fixed, it counts as fixed
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that since that column is allowed to be fixed, it is treated as already fixed, so it saves the scroll.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: since it is allowed to be fixed, it is considered fixed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers that a column with three errors still saves the scroll.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three errors on a column is within the fixable range. So we look at that column as if it were already corrected, which makes it a 'complete' column. That one column then saves the whole scroll.

keyTerms.meaning: It was given to be fixed, it is allowed to be fixed
It is fixed, it counts as fixed

phrases.english: He said to him:
Since it was given to be fixed, it is fixed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וְאִיתְיְהֵיב לְאִיתְּקוֹנֵי מִיתְּקַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A column with three errors can be fixed, so it counts as complete and saves the scroll.

steps.title: The limit applies only to missing letters, not extra ones
steps.stepSummary: The limit on mistakes applies only to missing letters. Extra letters are no problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies to missing letters. But extra letters are no problem for us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the whole error limit. It counts only letters that were left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A missing letter has to be squeezed in. An extra letter can simply be erased. So only missing letters count toward the limit that sends a scroll to גניזה.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply (only to...), a phrase that limits a rule
We have no problem with it

phrases.english: And these words apply to missing letters,
but extra letters, we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי חֲסֵירוֹת אֲבָל יְתֵירוֹת לֵית לַן בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines which mistakes count toward the error limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only missing letters count toward the limit. Extra letters do not.

steps.title: Why are missing letters a problem?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a scroll with many missing letters may not be fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Missing letters, what is the reason they may not be fixed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the difference made in step 41.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Missing letters can also be written in, so it seems the scroll could be fixed. The גמרא asks what is wrong with doing that.

phrases.english: Missing letters, what is the reason not?

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲסֵירוֹת מַאי טַעְמָא לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 41.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a scroll with many missing letters cannot simply be fixed.

steps.title: Because it would look speckled
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא explains that adding many missing letters between the lines makes the scroll look spotted (מנומר).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: because it looks speckled.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא gives the reason: so many letters squeezed in would make the scroll look messy and spotted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Missing letters have to be added between the lines. With many of them on every column, the scroll looks blotchy, which is not fitting for a ספר תורה. Erasing extra letters does not cause this, so extra letters are fine.
steps.whatToRemember: A ספר תורה with too many mistakes is put away only because of missing letters. Adding them between the lines would make it look spotted (מנומר). Extra letters can just be erased.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
Because it looks speckled.
phrases.notes: He means all the letters squeezed in between the lines would make the scroll look spotted.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּמִיחֲזֵי כִּמְנוּמָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 42.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Adding many missing letters between the lines makes the scroll look spotted (מנומר).

steps.title: Agra's scroll with extra letters
steps.stepSummary: אגרא, the father-in-law of רבי אבא, had many extra letters in his scroll. רבי אבא ruled that the strict rule applies only to missing letters, so his scroll may be fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אגרא, the father-in-law of רבי אבא, had extra letters in his scroll. He came to רבי אבא to ask what to do. רבי אבא told him: We only said the strict rule (that a scroll with many mistakes may not be fixed) about missing letters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story where רבי אבא applies the rule from step 41 to a practical case: a scroll full of extra letters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strict rule exists because adding many missing letters between the lines makes the scroll look spotted (step 43). Extra letters are simply erased, so nothing is squeezed between the lines and the scroll does not look spotted. That is why רבי אבא allows אגרא's scroll to be fixed even though it had many mistakes.

keyTerms.meaning: Extra letters, letters written that should not be there; they can be erased.
Missing letters, letters left out that must be added in.
We only said this about, a phrase that limits a rule to a specific case.

steps.whatToRemember: Many extra letters do not disqualify a scroll from being fixed. Only many missing letters are a problem, because adding them makes the scroll look spotted.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of mistakes. An extra letter is fixed by erasing it, which is fine. A missing letter must be squeezed in, and that is what the strict rule is about.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story shows that the rule from step 41 is real practical הלכה. A scribe with a scroll full of extra letters can simply erase them and use the scroll.

phrases.english: Agra, the father-in-law of Rabbi Abba,
had extra letters in his scroll.
He came before Rabbi Abba.
He said to him: We did not say it
phrases.notes: He means the rule that a scroll with too many mistakes may not be fixed.

phrases.english: except about missing letters.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַגְרָא חֲמוּהּ דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא הֲוָה לֵיהּ יְתֵירוֹת בְּסִיפְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the rule from step 41 (extra letters are no problem) being applied in a real case, building on the reason given in step 43.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule against fixing a scroll with many mistakes applies only to missing letters. A scroll with many extra letters may be fixed by erasing them.
